thf.name: THF (Tetrahydrofuran)
thf.practical: Grignard, NaH, Low-temp reactions, Enolate formation
thf.drying: Sodium/Benzophenone (Blue indicates dry) or 3Å Molecular Sieves
thf.risk: Peroxide former (Highly explosive when concentrated), Highly Flammable
thf.scaleup: Peroxide monitoring mandatory for bulk use. High volatility may cause pressure build-up.

dcm.name: DCM (Dichloromethane)
dcm.risk: Volatile, Suspected Carcinogen, Toxic (Metabolized to CO)
dcm.scaleup: Very low BP leads to high loss and inhalation risk. High density causes emulsion/separation issues in large reactors.

dmf.name: DMF (N,N-Dimethylformamide)
dmf.risk: Reprotoxic, Skin absorption (Rapidly carries solutes through skin)
dmf.scaleup: High BP makes removal difficult (requires vacuum distillation or multi-wash workup). Runaway risk with NaH > 60°C.

nah.name: NaH (Sodium Hydride, 60% dispersion)
nah.quench: IPA (Slowly) -> MeOH -> H2O (Sequence is critical to manage heat and H2 gas)
nah.risk: Water Reactive, Massive Hydrogen Evolution, Pyrophoric powder
nah.scaleup: Exothermic and H2 gas generation can be dangerous in large batches. Internal temp monitoring is mandatory.
nah.common_mistake: Using DMF at high temp (can lead to decomposition and explosion). Using water directly to quench.

nbuli.name: n-BuLi (n-Butyllithium)
nbuli.practical: Generation of LDA, Aryl lithiation, Anionic polymerization
nbuli.risk: Pyrophoric (Ignites on contact with air), Water Reactive
nbuli.scaleup: Extremely dangerous. Requires specialized flow chemistry or cannula transfer at scale. Pyrophoric leaks cause major fires.
nbuli.common_mistake: Exposure to air during transfer. Quenching too fast.

pdc.name: Pd/C (Palladium on Carbon, 5-10%)
pdc.practical: C=C reduction, Benzyl deprotection, Nitro reduction
pdc.quench: Filter through Celite wet. Wash with MeOH/Water. Do NOT let it dry.
pdc.risk: Pyrophoric when dry (especially after absorbing H2)
pdc.scaleup: Auto-ignition risk during filtration. Use 'Wet' catalyst (Degussa type). Inert gas blanket (Ar/N2) mandatory.
pdc.common_mistake: Adding dry Pd/C directly to flammable solvents. Allowing the filter cake to dry.

dmso.name: DMSO (Dimethyl Sulfoxide)
dmso.practical: Swern oxidation, Finkelstein reaction, NMR solvent
dmso.risk: Low acute toxicity, but carries toxins through skin. High freezing point (18°C).
dmso.scaleup: Extremely hard to remove (BP 189°C). Requires massive water washes. Odor issues (Dimethyl sulfide byproduct).
dmso.incompatible: Sodium hydride (dimsyl salt formation is exothermic), Strong oxidizers

mecn.name: Acetonitrile (MeCN)
mecn.scaleup: Relatively safe and easy to remove. Azeotrope with water makes drying difficult if wet.

boc2o.name: Boc2O (Di-tert-butyl dicarbonate)
boc2o.risk: Toxic by inhalation (Vapor), Low melting point (~23°C)
boc2o.scaleup: CO2 gas evolution during protection. Pressure management is key.
boc2o.common_mistake: Not accounting for CO2 volume in closed systems.

tfa.name: TFA (Trifluoroacetic acid)
tfa.practical: Boc deprotection, PMB cleavage, NMR additive
tfa.risk: Highly Corrosive, Toxic, Persistent in environment
tfa.scaleup: Extreme corrosiveness requires Hastelloy or glass-lined reactors. Gas evolution (Isobutylene) during Boc cleavage.
tfa.ich: Not listed (usually treated as Class 2/3 equivalent)

liah4.name: LiAlH4 (LAH, Lithium Aluminum Hydride)
liah4.practical: Reduction of esters, amides, acids to alcohols/amines
liah4.quench: Fieser Method: n g LAH -> n mL H2O -> n mL 15% NaOH -> 3n mL H2O. Sequence is vital.
liah4.risk: Water Reactive, Pyrophoric, Massive H2 evolution
liah4.scaleup: Extremely exothermic quench. Requires jacketed reactor and very slow addition of quench agents. Dry THF/Ether mandatory.
liah4.common_mistake: Using wet solvents. Quencing with water too fast.

nabh4.name: NaBH4 (Sodium Borohydride)
nabh4.practical: Reduction of aldehydes and ketones to alcohols
nabh4.quench: Slow addition of dilute acid (HCl) or water
nabh4.scaleup: Safe alternative to LAH. Still generates H2, so headspace ventilation is needed.
nabh4.common_mistake: Adding acid too quickly (foam-over due to H2).

lda.name: LDA (Lithium Diisopropylamide)
lda.quench: Slow addition of water or NH4Cl (aq) at low temp
lda.scaleup: Usually generated in-situ (n-BuLi + DIPA). Requires strict temp control (-78°C to 0°C).

tbuok.name: t-BuOK (Potassium tert-butoxide)
tbuok.scaleup: Very hygroscopic. Clumping in feeders causes issues. Strong heat of neutralization.
tbuok.common_mistake: Using old, yellow/brown material (decomposed to K2CO3/t-BuOH).

socl2.name: SOCl2 (Thionyl Chloride)
socl2.quench: Slow addition to cold water or NaOH solution (Exothermic + Gas)
socl2.risk: Toxic, Corrosive, Water Reactive, Pungent odor
socl2.scaleup: Generates SO2 and HCl gas. Scrubber system is absolute requirement. Distillation at scale is hazardous.
socl2.common_mistake: Not using a trap/scrubber. Adding to water too fast.

pocc3.name: POCl3 (Phosphorus Oxychloride)
pocc3.quench: Very slow addition to cold water or basic solution
pocc3.scaleup: Highly exothermic hydrolysis. Potential for 'delayed' quench (induction period followed by explosion).

mcpba.name: mCPBA (meta-Chloroperoxybenzoic acid)
mcpba.quench: Sodium thiosulfate (Na2S2O3) or NaHSO3 to destroy excess peroxide
mcpba.scaleup: Shock sensitive if dry. Usually sold as ~75% wet with water for safety. Exothermic decomposition.

edc.name: EDC·HCl (1-Ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide)
edc.scaleup: Preferred over DCC for scale-up because byproduct (urea) is easily removed by water wash.
edc.common_mistake: Using in anhydrous-only reactions (it works, but byproduct removal needs water).

dipea.name: DIPEA (Hünig's Base)
dipea.scaleup: High recovery potential due to BP (~127°C). Less nucleophilic than Et3N, minimizing side reactions.

et3n.name: Et3N (Triethylamine)
et3n.scaleup: Cheap and easy to remove (BP 89°C). Forms salts (Et3NHCl) that can cause slurry issues.

2methf.name: 2-MeTHF (2-Methyltetrahydrofuran)
2methf.risk: Flammable, Peroxide former (but slower than THF)
2methf.scaleup: Derived from renewable sources (corn cobs). Limited water miscibility (easier workup/phase separation than THF).

cpme.name: CPME (Cyclopentyl Methyl Ether)
cpme.risk: Flammable, Low peroxide formation risk compared to THF
cpme.scaleup: High BP (106°C) and low water solubility make it excellent for azeotropic drying and easy workup.
